treaty_name: Convention between the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg for the elimination of double taxation with respect to taxes on income and on capital and the prevention of tax avoidance and evasion (2022)
eif_quote: ARTICLE 29 ... This Convention shall enter into force on the date of receipt of the later notification and shall thereupon have effect: ... b) in Luxembourg: (i) in respect of taxes withheld at source, to income derived on or after 1 January of the calendar year next following the year in which the Convention enters into force (LU list: 'Mémorial A N° 632 du 4 octobre 2023 à partir du 01.01.2024')
source_title: UK–LU Convention signed 7 June 2022 – English signed text (Luxembourg ACD)

rates.quote: 2. However, dividends paid by a company which is a resident of a Contracting State may also be taxed in that State according to the laws of that State, but if the beneficial owner of the dividends is a resident of the other Contracting State: a) except as provided in sub-paragraph b), such dividends shall be exempt from tax in the Contracting State of which the company paying the dividends is a resident;
1. Interest arising in a Contracting State and beneficially owned by a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State.
1. Royalties arising in a Contracting State and beneficially owned by a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State.

ppt.quote: 1. Notwithstanding the other provisions of this Convention, a benefit under this Convention shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital, or a capital gain, if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless ...

notes: Dividends exempt at source (Art. 10(2)(a)) except Art. 10(2)(b): dividends paid out of income/gains from immovable property by an investment vehicle that distributes most of this income annually and whose immovable-property income is tax-exempt (e.g. UK REIT/PAIF) — capped at 15%, unless the beneficial owner is a recognised pension fund (then exempt). REIT tier not modelled as a general tier. The 1967 Convention (as amended) ceased to have effect from the dates the 2022 Convention took effect. MLI does not apply to the 2022 Convention; PPT is in the treaty itself. EIF date from treaty-map dataset.
